title: Mandate 84: Susi core stays under 100,000 lines and never grows
goal: Vision: V-9. CEO directive 2026-11-16: susi core should always be under 100k lines. Record it as CEO Mandate 84 (constitution entry, docs/ceo-mandate-84.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md, README, self-build contract) on the counting contract of Vision V-6, and make it hold: pin the complete socket's measured size as a ceiling in tests/lean_core_ceilings.rs that only goes down, so core cannot grow while it is above 100,000 and cannot pass 99,999 once below. The CEO's words and the commercial edition are in intellibitz/susi-commercial-apps (its T-AGENTCLAUDECORE100K-1).

reuse.searched: Vision V-6 and its program (docs/lean-core.md 'Complete socket below 100,000 lines', task T-CODEXCORE100K-1), the size measure already in tests/lean_core_ceilings.rs (repository_size, the ignored complete_socket_is_under_100k_lines acceptance check run by cargo core-size), the dependency-reach ceilings that only go down in the same file, core's fast release pipeline that runs that suite (xtask/src/fast_release.rs), and the mandate records of Mandates 69, 78, 82 and 83. The mandate reuses V-6's counting contract and the existing measure; the only new code is one pinned constant and one assertion in the same test file. No dependency or harvest.

limitations: Core is not under 100,000 lines: the complete socket measures 307,737 on 2026-11-16. The mandate makes it stop growing now; getting under is the V-6 reduction program (T-CODEXCORE100K-1).

The ceiling is enforced by the lean_core_ceilings suite (ordinary test run and fast release pipeline), not by a hook: main stays ungated (Mandate 74), so a growing commit can land on main and is refused at the next test run and release.
Nothing checks that a shrinking change lowered the ceiling; the test prints the value to pin.
'No functionality dropped' and 'no tricks' are verified by review, regression and conformance runs, not by the count.
The counting contract is V-6's (runtime Rust plus facades); the CEO's words did not name what counts, and tests, tooling and vendor/ are reported but not counted.
